nodes.claim: A(O)=((κ+1)/2)I-((κ-1)/4)(O+Oᵀ); n≥3, κ≥4; O ranges over full O(n).
p(O,x)=sqrt(det A(O))/(2π)^((n:ℝ)/2) * exp(-xᵀA(O)x/2) is the literal real expression in the signature. It is not a newly chosen density or Gaussian measure.
Finite real O(n) with its matrix subspace topology is a compact topological group with canonical Borel measurable structure; matrix inclusion, multiplication and transpose/inverse are continuous.
For Q∈O(n), QᵀQ=QQᵀ=I, transpose is inverse, conjugation c_Q(O)=QOQᵀ belongs to O(n), and c_(Qᵀ) is inverse to c_Q.
c_Q is a continuous group automorphism and Borel measurable homeomorphism.
μ is the actual normalized Haar probability on full O(n), with μ(O(n))=1 and hence finite measure. It is not Haar restricted to SO(n), a point mass, or a caller-supplied invariant functional.
(c_Q)_*μ=μ. A continuous group automorphism sends normalized Haar to normalized Haar, so uniqueness proves conjugation invariance (equivalently use compact-group left and right Haar invariance).
det(Qᵀ)=det(Q), det(Q)²=1 and det(O)∈{-1,1}; determinant multiplicativity yields det(c_Q(O))=det(O), including orientation-reversing Q and O.
A(c_Q(O))=Q A(O) Qᵀ, by expanding Eq4, transpose of products, distributivity and orthogonality.
det A(c_Q(O))=det A(O) using R08 and det(Q)²=1; therefore their real square roots agree. No Gaussian normalization theorem is needed.
(Qx)ᵀ A(c_Q(O)) (Qx)=xᵀ A(O)x using R08 and QᵀQ=I; coordinate dotProduct and mulVec express this same quadratic identity.
p(c_Q(O),Qx)=p(O,x), obtained by substituting R09 and R10 into the fixed literal formula.
For every fixed x, O↦A(O), det A(O), xᵀA(O)x and det(O) are continuous: finite coordinate sums/products, transpose, determinant and evaluation are continuous.

For every fixed x, O↦p(O,x) and f_x(O)=det(O)p(O,x) are continuous, using continuous real sqrt and exp, multiplication and a fixed denominator. (2π)^((n:ℝ)/2)>0 is an elementary scalar fact, not a density normalizer premise.
Continuity on compact O(n) makes f_x Borel/strongly measurable and bounded in absolute value for each fixed x. The bound may depend on x, n and κ; no spatial uniform integrable majorant is asserted.
For every fixed x, f_x is genuinely L1(μ): bounded measurable real function plus μ(O(n))=1 implies ∫|f_x|dμ<∞. This supplies the explicit Integrable conjunct and applies also at Qx.
Haar change of variables gives ∫f_(Qx)(O)dμ(O)=∫f_(Qx)(c_Q(O))dμ(O), justified by R06, measurability and genuine L1.
f_(Qx)(c_Q(O))=f_x(O) pointwise by determinant-sign preservation and literal-formula covariance.
For every fixed Q∈O(n) and x∈ℝⁿ, ∫det(O)p(O,Qx)dμ=∫det(O)p(O,x)dμ. This is the rotation-invariance step underlying Ex58, not Ex58's norm-axis identification.
Combine ∀x Integrable f_x μ with ∀Q ∀x signed-kernel rotation invariance, under only the stated standing n≥3 and κ≥4 hypotheses and literal local let.
